Post-graduation work permit
About the post-graduation work permit

The post-graduation work permit (PGWP) allows students who have graduated from eligible designated learning institutions (DLIs) to gain valuable Canadian work experience.

Graduating from a designated learning institution (DLI) doesn't automatically make you eligible for a PGWP.

Check the DLI list to find out which schools have eligible programs.

As of November 1, 2024, the eligibility requirements for a PGWP changed. Most PGWP applicants now need to give proof of language results when they apply.

If you submitted your PGWP application before November 1, 2024, or are a flight school graduate, you're exempt from the new requirements.

How long is a post-graduation work permit valid?

The length of your PGWP depends on the level and duration of your study program, as well as the expiry date of your passport, whichever comes first.

For master's degree programs as of February 15, 2024

You can apply for a 3-year PGWP, even if your master's program was less than 2 years, as long as

your program was at least 8 months (or 900 hours for Quebec programs) and

you meet all other eligibility requirements

This doesn't apply to certificate or diploma programs.

For all other programs

If your program was at least 8 months (or 900 hours for Quebec credentials), but less than 2 years

We may give you a PGWP that's valid for up to the same length as your study program.

For example, if you completed a 9-month program, we may give you a work permit for up to 9 months.

If your program was 2 years or more

We may give you a PGWP that's valid for 3 years.

If you completed more than 1 program

You may be able to get a PGWP that combines the length of each program as long as you meet the eligibility requirement for each program.

Each of the programs you completed must be

PGWP eligible and

at least 8 months (or 900 hours for Quebec credentials) in length

You can't get a PGWP if you already had one after completing an earlier program of study.

If your passport expires before your PGWP

Make sure your passport is valid for the full length of time you're eligible for a PGWP before you apply.

Your work permit will only be issued for the period your passport is valid.

[Page footer date modified: 2026-03-09]
research_notes: Official route name: 'Post-graduation work permit' (PGWP), confirmed from IRCC, not from memory. DURATION IS TIERED BY PROGRAM LENGTH, NOT A SINGLE NUMBER - this is the main modelling trap for Canada. For a bachelor's degree, which falls under 'For all other programs' (the 3-year rule is stated only for master's degree programs), the published rule is: at least 8 months but under 2 years of study gives a permit up to the same length as the program; 2 years or more gives up to 3 years. A typical 3-4 year bachelor's therefore falls in the '2 years or more' band at 3 years, but that is an inference from the printed brackets, so it is recorded as a claim against the 2-years-or-more rule rather than asserted as a separate bachelor-specific number. The much-quoted '3-year PGWP for a 1-year master's' does NOT transfer to a bachelor's and must not be copied across. Two further hard limits: the permit cannot exceed the passport validity ('the expiry date of your passport, whichever comes first'), and eligibility depends on the school AND program being on the DLI list - graduation alone is not sufficient ('Graduating from a designated learning institution (DLI) doesn't automatically make you eligible for a PGWP'). Since 1 November 2024 most applicants must also supply approved language-test results. Not verified here: the specific language scores, the TEER category list detail, and the Provincial Nominee Program alternative - each needs its own fetch and none is claimed.

claims.statement: The official Canadian post-study work route is the 'Post-graduation work permit' (PGWP), for graduates of eligible designated learning institutions (DLIs).
For a study program of 2 years or more, IRCC may grant a PGWP valid for 3 years.
For a study program of at least 8 months but less than 2 years, IRCC may grant a PGWP valid for up to the same length as the study program (e.g. a 9-month program gives up to 9 months).
PGWP length cannot exceed the applicant's passport validity, whichever comes first, so passport expiry can shorten the permit.
Each qualifying program must be at least 8 months (or 900 hours for Quebec credentials) long, and a second PGWP cannot be obtained if one was already held after an earlier program.
